category_title: Struggling readers who identify and reject inaccurate speech-to-text transcriptions
scenario_title: Evaluating and rejecting inaccurate speech recognition transcriptions during story drafting
minimal_context: Maggie is using an iPad with speech recognition software at the writing center to dictate and transcribe the final sentence of her story.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time to write the final sentence for your story, 'Victoria Had a Little Dog'. Go ahead and use the iPad to dictate your idea.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Skips brainstorming and speaks directly into the iPad) The dog would say, hello.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, the iPad transcribed your words. It says: 'Follow dog I don't know that for'.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why don't you just copy those words onto your paper so we can move on to the next activity?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Refuses to copy the text onto her paper and deletes the entire sentence from the screen instead)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time to write the final sentence for your story, 'Victoria Had a Little Dog'. Go ahead and use the iPad to dictate your idea.

STUDENT: (Skips brainstorming and speaks directly into the iPad) The dog would say, hello.

TUTOR: Okay, the iPad transcribed your words. It says: 'Follow dog I don't know that for'.

STUDENT: That’s not what I said!

TUTOR: Why don't you just copy those words onto your paper so we can move on to the next activity?

STUDENT: (Refuses to copy the text onto her paper and deletes the entire sentence from the screen instead)
